methodological_rigor.justification: Multicenter retrospective cohort study (195 patients from 3 institutions in Côte d'Ivoire) with binary logistic regression for associations with pCR and Cox regression for survival analysis. Kaplan-Meier survival curves with log-rank test comparisons. Appropriate outcome definitions (pCR, ORR, PFS, OS) and molecular subtype categorization by IHC. However, retrospective design, single-country cohort, and no prospective validation. Exclusion criteria appropriate (surgery delay >12 weeks, follow-up <1 year); 43 patients excluded for criteria, resulting in 195 analyzable.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: LoE 4 (observational case series with outcome analysis). Direct clinical relevance: pCR achieved in 28.7%, associated with significantly better 5-year PFS (96.1% vs 57.7%) and OS (95% vs 71.6%). Demonstrates pCR as strongest independent predictor of PFS (HR 6.54) and OS (HR 5.84). Findings support pCR as surrogate for survival in Black African breast cancer population—clinically actionable for treatment decisions.

reporting_quality.justification: STROBE guidelines followed: objectives, patient selection, data collection, molecular subtype categorization detailed. Outcome definitions clear (pCR per AJCC, PFS, OS). Baseline characteristics presented (Table I); binary logistic regression results with OR and 95% CIs; multivariate analysis table provided. However, no data availability statement; no supplementary data or raw data deposition mentioned.

novelty_literature.justification: pCR as prognostic factor in breast cancer known from developed country studies. Present study confirms finding in Black African population—addresses gap in published data ('to best of our knowledge...not yet studied'). Contribution is validation in underrepresented population rather than methodological novelty.

writing_presentation.justification: Well-organized with clear introduction motivating racial/ethnic disparities, methods with inclusion/exclusion criteria detailed, results with appropriate tables and Kaplan-Meier curves. Discussion contextualizes within breast cancer literature and emphasizes underrepresentation of African patient data. Generally clear; some sections could be more concise.

key_strengths: Addresses important gap: first study of pCR prognostic value in Black African breast cancer population.
Strong clinical outcomes: pCR achieves 96.1% 5-year PFS and 95% 5-year OS in CR patients.
Multivariate analysis confirms pCR as strongest predictor (HR 6.54 for PFS, HR 5.84 for OS).
Multicenter design (3 institutions) strengthens generalizability within region.
Appropriate molecular subtype analysis demonstrating HER2-positive higher pCR (OR 2.62) and OS benefit in TN subtype.
key_concerns: Retrospective single-country design; limited to Côte d'Ivoire (generalizability to broader African/diaspora populations unclear).
No prospective validation; potential for unmeasured confounding.
43 patients excluded (18% attrition); reasons for follow-up loss not detailed.
Median follow-up 49.4 months; some patients <5 years follow-up may affect OS estimates.
No adjusted analyses for socioeconomic factors, treatment delays, or comorbidities that may differ in African setting.
Single timepoint (post-NAC pCR); longitudinal response data not captured.
chief_reviewer.rationale: Solid multicenter retrospective study confirming strong prognostic value of pCR in Black African breast cancer patients, addressing important evidence gap. Clinically relevant with good survival outcomes. Retrospective design and single-country scope warrant minor revisions for clarity on follow-up/exclusions. Appropriate for tier 3 journals given clinical relevance and population focus.
